insights: Callbacks own captured strings and mapped/open file data; stream commit has an explicit exactly-once lifecycle. Ink immutable input snapshots should likewise survive later path changes.

Ordinary cache writes finish a temporary file in the destination directory and publish by rename. The open file is obtained before publication to survive concurrent pruning. Both Ink planner caches already use same-directory temporary replacement.
An expected absent/deleting file can be a cache miss. Ink compiled_cache has an uncaught inventory/stat deletion race also previously repaired in plan_cache; reproduce and share that implementation.

Windows rename-permission fallback returns a copy of newly written bytes instead of reopening a path a pruner may remove. Do not generalize that policy to arbitrary errors or mathematical proof admission.
MoveFileToCache cross-device path copies directly; it is a separate behavior from temporary-stream atomic replacement. No inference of identical guarantees across modes.

Provided LLVM tests cover normal hits, closed output after commit and death on uncommitted destruction. They do not establish concurrent-pruning, Windows fallback or cross-device correctness. No LLVM code was copied.
application: F034 reproducible cache IO repairs; F033 sealed in-memory proof reuse is a different trust boundary and cannot use a disk-cache hit as proof.
